name: Silicon photonics and optical interconnects
summary: Light carries data between chips and systems to relieve the energy and bandwidth limits of electrical connections.
useCase: A large AI cluster uses optical links and eventually optics closer to the processor to move data across thousands of accelerators.
whyNow: AI clusters place heavy demands on interconnect bandwidth and energy. Commercial transceivers are established, while co-packaged optics and optical input/output remain at earlier stages. Coherent’s Data Center and Communications revenue provides an observable adjacent-market signal: about US$2.63 billion in fiscal 2024, US$3.76 billion in 2025 and US$5.27 billion in 2026. Most of that cannot be labeled new silicon-photonics adoption.

mainstream.scope: Co-packaged optics and optical I/O used routinely in the largest bandwidth-constrained AI and cloud systems.
mainstream.rationale: Bandwidth economics and current supplier investment support deployment this decade. Mature pluggable optics remain a strong alternative, so the transition depends on reliability, manufacturability and serviceability rather than technical demonstrations alone. Enterprise-wide optical chip-to-chip interconnects could arrive later than hyperscale use.

direction: Accelerating from components toward integrated systems

metric.name: Coherent Data Center and Communications revenue — adjacent proxy
metric.scope: Coherent’s reported segment, including established optical communications products; fiscal years end in June.
metric.growthLabel: Segment revenue roughly doubled from FY2024 to FY2026
metric.limitations: This is a broad optical-communications supplier segment, not the size of the silicon-photonics or co-packaged-optics market. The series uses the comparable segment presentation in the FY2026 filing. It reflects price, mix and demand as well as units.
metric.futureNote: No comparable external segment-revenue forecast is used. Follow qualified co-packaged products, port shipments and energy per bit to see whether the technical transition becomes economic.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable optical-I/O shipment count identified; conventional fiber links were already established.
No harmonized commercial co-packaged-optics adoption metric supplied.
No comparable market-wide annual deployment measurement identified.
Coherent’s comparable segment recorded US$2.63 billion revenue, an adjacent demand measure.
Coherent reported initial 1.6T transceiver revenue shipments and US$3.76 billion segment revenue.
The segment reached US$5.27 billion; Ayar Labs expanded its announced 2026 funding to US$650 million.

tailwinds: Larger AI clusters reward bandwidth density and lower energy per transmitted bit.
Foundry, packaging, laser and networking ecosystems are investing in integrated optical systems.
bottlenecks: Laser integration, thermal behavior, packaging yield and optical alignment must work at manufacturing scale.
Replacing serviceable pluggable modules changes maintenance and system-repair economics.
watchMetrics: Energy per bit and delivered bandwidth at equal link length and reliability.
Revenue-bearing co-packaged-optics port shipments and field failure rates, separate from sampling announcements.
